newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INSTANT VIEW - Malaysia posts smaller deficit in '96.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Malaysia posts smaller deficit in '96.

text.p: Following are economists' initial reactions to Malaysia's reporting of a 617.97 million ringgit trade deficit in 1996, against a 9.36 billion ringgit gap in 1995:
LIEW YIN SZE, CHIEF ECONOMIST AT J.M. SASSOON & CO
The current account figure (released on Saturday) was slightly better than forecast, so the December surplus (of 872 million ringgit) is slightly above expectations.
My view is that the improvement in 1997 will be harder to come by. I think they have tried to hold back some of the imports last year because of the current account.
But as the Commonwealth Games (in 1998) nears, they have to import (equipment for finishing the Commonwealth Games projects).

Imports also tend to accelerate faster in a recovery of the manufacturing sector. I think this will happen in 1997. Things will deteriorate more in 1997, but as a percentage of GNP, I don't think the current account will be much worse.
KEVIN CHEW, ECONOMIST AT CASPIAN SECURITIES
This is better than what people are looking at.
It could be seen as positive for the currency market.
Looking ahead, I personally think economic growth will be stronger this year (at 8.4 percent), based on expectations that investments will be stronger.
I think import demand will be quite strong for 1997 but exports will also recover as electronics rebound.
